units.oneLiner: Keep every key in the slot array itself and, when the home slot is taken, probe the next slot and the next: the probes stay inside the cache line the first one fetched, Knuth's 1963 formulas say exactly what each load factor costs, and the price is clustering, which is why the table resizes before it is full and why the hash must scatter neighbors.
units.description: Linear probing on 65,536 slots against Knuth's 1963 formulas (within 1% to load 0.7) and a Python set over 1,200,000 operations: at load 0.9 a hit costs 5.315 probes but 1.540 cache lines against 2.570 and 2.570 for double hashing; clusters of 715 slots; tombstones 5.864 probes per miss against 1.698 for backward shift; a weak hash costs 1,056 probes per hit.
units.time: O(1) expected; (1 + 1/(1 - a)) / 2 probes per hit

narration_plan.release: not generated yet (generate right before publication)

units.plan_row: Open addressing × Linear probing. Puzzle 172, data-structures (problemSlug hash-collision-resolution, the atlas problem page carrying "Cache-friendly hashing"; sibling live lesson cuckoo-hashing-two-table-eviction-kicks). Solution open_addressing_linear_probing.py (3.0s, prints OK): linear probing with tombstone or backward-shift deletion and a rebuild at 85% live-plus-tombstones, quadratic probing (triangular offsets), double hashing (odd stride), separate chaining, Robin Hood, Fibonacci and weak hashes, a probe-and-cache-line counter (8 slots per 64-byte line, one line per chaining node). ORACLES: (1) Knuth 1963 at loads 0.25 / 0.5 / 0.7 / 0.8 / 0.9 / 0.95: hits 1.164 / 1.509 / 2.172 / 3.027 / 5.962 / 11.609 against 1.167 / 1.500 / 2.167 / 3.000 / 5.500 / 10.500, misses 1.397 / 2.510 / 5.971 / 12.655 / 50.434 / 205.639 against 1.389 / 2.500 / 6.056 / 13.000 / 50.500 / 200.500 (within 6% to 0.8, 20% beyond); (2) 1,200,000 mixed operations across six structures all matching a Python set, final sizes matching; (3) the race at load 0.9 (every key looked up, 5,000 misses): linear probing 5.315 probes/hit, 47.975/miss, 1.540 lines/hit, variance 277, max 612, longest cluster 715; Robin Hood 5.315 / 5.644 / 1.540 / 19.8 / 29; quadratic 2.850 / 12.055 / 1.951 / 16.2 / 92; double hashing 2.570 / 10.056 / 2.570 / 11.1 / 68; chaining 2.450 / 1.923 / 2.450 / 0.5 / 9; longest run by load 8 / 31 / 85 / 209 / 752 / 3,250; (4) deletion: fill to 0.7, delete half: tombstones 5.864 probes per miss (formula for 0.7: 6.056), backward shift 1.698 (formula for 0.35: 1.683); (5) weak hash (high bits) on 2,048 consecutive keys in 4,096 slots: linear probing 1,056 probes per hit, double hashing 8.3, chaining 402.8, strong hash 1.50. Honest: linear probing pays twice double hashing's probes at 0.9 and wins only on lines; the Robin Hood mean is identical to 1e-9 (the displacement total is invariant), asserted; three author notes recorded (quadratic vs double ordering; the first weak-hash experiment at 65,536 slots ran quadratic for ten minutes and was shrunk; a 5,000-key hit sample was replaced by every key after the early-inserted keys biased it). Cards: self, Hash table with chaining, Robin Hood hashing, Cuckoo hashing (live lesson badge) (all algoName). neverUse: linear probing with a hash that keeps neighbors neighbors. Figure: Knuth's hit and miss curves with the measured points beside bars of the longest run by load; cite Knuth 1963 / TAOCP 3 6.4, Amdahl et al. 1954, Pagh-Pagh-Ruzic STOC 2007 DOI 10.1145/1250790.1250839. Viz LinearProbingViz: a 64-slot table as eight cache lines filling to load 0.9, walked slots amber and touched lines outlined, the running average probes per insert against Knuth's expectation, every key checked reachable from its home each tick; NODE-VERIFIED 20 cycles x 21 ticks, 0 breaks; stepMs 500, holdTicks rests. Preserved narration: Aoede + Algieba.

units.oneLiner: Scan the pixels once in reading order, giving each foreground pixel the label of a neighbor already seen or a fresh one, record every meeting of two labels as a union, then rewrite each label to its root in a second pass: two streaming reads, no stack, no recursion, and a merge-only table sized by labels, not pixels.
units.description: Two-pass labeling against a flood-fill referee: equal partitions on 88 image-connectivity pairs; 38,400 visits (two per pixel) against 41,280 and 63,360; 179 and 78 provisional labels for 28 and 27 blobs merged by 151 and 51 unions at 0.635 and 0.405 links per find; a 3,220-pixel snake crashes a recursive fill; the naive single pass splits every U.
units.time: O(n α(n)): two passes over n pixels, near-constant per union and find
units.space: O(L) parent and rank entries for L provisional labels, plus the label image
units.baseline: Breadth-first flood fill from every unlabeled pixel
units.plan_row: Connected component labeling × Two-pass union-find. Puzzle 190, signal-graphics (problemSlug region-labeling, the atlas problem page carrying "Region labeling"; sibling live lessons canny-edge-detector-hysteresis-thresholding, puzzle 173, and unionfind-rank-compression, puzzle 8). Solution connected_component_labeling_two_pass_union_find.py (0.3s, prints OK): a counting union-find (unions, finds, parent links followed) with path compression and union by rank, the two-pass labeler (visits, provisional labels), an iterative BFS flood fill (visits, queue maximum), a recursive flood fill (max depth, RecursionError reported instead of crashing), run-length labeling, union-find over raw pixels, the naive single pass, and image builders (random disks, separated disks, a one-pixel-wide snake, U shapes, diagonal stripes). ORACLES: (1) partition equality (never label numbers) against the BFS on a 160 x 120 image of 60 disks (5,520 foreground pixels) under 4- and 8-connectivity, on 40 random 64 x 48 images under both (80 pairs), and on 10, 25, and 40 separated disks whose counts are known by construction: 88 comparisons, with run-length labeling and pixel union-find agreeing too; (2) counts: 28 / 27 components; two-pass 38,400 visits (exactly 2 per pixel, asserted) against BFS 41,280 / 63,360 (queue max 30 / 50); provisional labels 179 / 78, unions 151 / 51, finds 7,934 / 7,474 at 0.635 / 0.405 links per find (asserted under 1.5); unions == sets made minus components asserted for every method; run-length 499 runs, 471 / 472 unions, 1,443 / 1,455 finds; pixel union-find 5,520 sets, 5,492 / 5,493 unions, 25,588 / 45,026 finds at 0.824 / 0.889 links; recursive fill 41,280 / 63,360 visits (equal to BFS, asserted), depth 597 / 573; (3) snake 160 x 40 (3,220 pixels, one component): two-pass 12,800 visits, 11 labels, 10 unions; BFS queue max 1; recursive fill depth 3,220 at limit 50,000 and RecursionError at the default 1,000 (asserted); (4) diagonal stripes 60 x 60 period 3: 1,200 components under 4-connectivity (every pixel alone), 39 under 8 (asserted against the stripe count); (5) negative example: naive single pass 60 labels for 30 U shapes (asserted at least 2 per U) and 78 for 27 blobs under 8-connectivity; the two-pass made the same 60 provisional labels and 30 unions on the U image. Honest: author correction recorded (the draft expected about one provisional label per component; measured several per blob, 179 for 28 under 4-connectivity, because every row where a blob widens on its left starts a label). Cards: self, Flood fill, Union-find (live lesson badge, puzzle 8), Run-length encoding (all algoName; pages verified in dist/algo). neverUse: one raster pass with no equivalence table (60 labels for 30 U shapes), with the recursive flood fill crash as its cousin. Figure: pass one on a U shape with labels 1 and 2 and the amber union at the corner, beside a log-scale chart of sets made and finds spent (two-pass 78 / 7,474; run-length 499 / 1,455; pixel union-find 5,520 / 45,026); cite Rosenfeld and Pfaltz JACM 1966 DOI 10.1145/321356.321357, He, Chao, Suzuki IEEE TIP 2008, Wu, Otoo, Suzuki PAA 2009. Viz ComponentLabelingViz: a seeded 48 x 16 image (disks, two U shapes, specks) under 4- or 8-connectivity per cycle; pass one six pixels per tick with provisional-label colors and an amber flash per union, pass two twelve per tick recoloring to final components; invariant every tick of pass one: the union-find classes over the scanned prefix equal an independent flood fill's components of that prefix; at the end partition equality with the full flood fill, visits == 2N, unions == labels minus components; NODE-VERIFIED 20 cycles x 191 ticks, 0 breaks; stepMs 60, holdTicks rests. Preserved narration: Aoede + Algieba (plan 27,604 billable characters, 10 provider requests, $0.828120, approval 9ea8d606...). units.oneLiner: Hash every integer lattice point to a unit gradient, make the surface zero there with that slope, and blend the four corner planes with the quintic fade 6t^5 - 15t^4 + 10t^3 so slope and curvature join across cells: a smooth, bounded, stateless texture at any point and scale, with octaves at halving amplitude for terrain.
units.description: Perlin noise on a 256 x 256 lattice: exactly 0 at 16,384 of 16,384 grid points with the hashed slope; inside the sqrt(2)/2 bound on 265,536 samples, attained in 28 cells; border slope jump 2.7e-9 (quintic) against 2.703 (linear crease); curvature step 12.5 for the 1985 cubic; 0.005% of the power above two cycles per cell.
units.time: O(2^n) corner gradients per sample (4 in 2D)
units.baseline: Value noise (random lattice heights, same fade)
units.plan_row: Perlin noise × Gradient lattice interpolation. Puzzle 191, signal-graphics (problemSlug procedural-texturing, the atlas problem page carrying "Procedural texturing"; atlas topic graphics-rendering, tier 1; first live unit of that topic). Solution perlin_noise_gradient_lattice_interpolation.py (0.5s, prints OK): a seeded Lattice class (permutation of 0 to 255 written twice, hash p[p[i & 255] + (j & 255)], eight unit gradients or a value in [-1, 1] per grid point, a corner-fetch counter as the work currency), 2-D Perlin noise with a pluggable fade (quintic 6t^5 - 15t^4 + 10t^3, Perlin's 1985 cubic 3t^2 - 2t^3, linear), value noise on the same lattice, white noise with one hash per sample, fractal Brownian motion, 2-D simplex noise, a recursive FFT, and helpers for power bands, median frequency, lag-one autocorrelation, zero crossings, and one-sided slope and curvature jumps. ORACLES: (1) exactly 0.0 at 16,384 of 16,384 lattice points; the central-difference slope there equals the hashed gradient to 1.0e-7, root-mean-square slope 1.000000 for Perlin against 5.7e-8 for value noise (every grid point of value noise is a stationary point); (2) the range bound sqrt(2)/2 = 0.707107 held at all 65,536 cell centers of the torus and 200,000 random points, attained exactly in 28 cells (5 with all four gradients pointing inward, 23 outward); mean -0.0007, standard deviation 0.2104; (3) across 2,000 cell borders the one-sided slope jump is 2.70e-9 (quintic), 8.13e-5 (cubic), 2.703 (linear, a crease; interior slopes reach 1.860), value noise 3.6e-9, simplex at random points 3.6e-4; the curvature jump is 0.1241 at h = 1e-3 and 0.0125 at 1e-4 for the quintic (shrinking: continuous curvature) against 12.4533 and 12.5148 for the cubic (a step: the 2002 improvement); (4) FFT of 4,096 samples (16 per cell) along lattice-periodic lines: Perlin on a generic line 41.7% of the power below a quarter cycle per cell, 58.3% between a quarter and two cycles, 0.005% above two, median frequency 0.301 cycles per cell, lag-one autocorrelation 0.9871, 0.82 zero crossings per cell; along a lattice row 6.1% / 93.9% / 0.010%, median 0.512; value noise 58.3% / 41.7% / 0.002%, median 0.199, lag-one 0.9929, 0.51 crossings; white noise 0.6% / 19.4% / 80.068%, median 4.000, lag-one -0.0658, 8.50 crossings; (5) corners per sample Perlin 4 against simplex 3 (simplex range [-0.705, +0.706] after its x70 scale); four octaves at halving amplitude inside the bound with standard deviations 0.2104, 0.1560, 0.1371, 0.1288 (max +0.6409, +0.4753, +0.4320, +0.4085). Two author corrections recorded in the file header: the draft wrote the range as [-1, 1] (the scaled range) where the raw bound is sqrt(2)/2, and the draft called the noise band-pass where a generic line carries two fifths of its power below a quarter cycle per cell (band-pass only along a lattice row), so the page says band-limited above. Cards: self, Simplex noise, Worley noise, Diamond-square algorithm (all algoName; pages verified in dist/algo). Baseline: value noise. neverUse: linear interpolation in place of the fade (the 2.703 crease), with white noise as the other trap. Contest table: six rows (quintic, cubic, linear, value noise, white noise, simplex) over grid-point behavior, border slope jump, power above two cycles per cell, median frequency, corners per sample. Figure: one-dimensional gradient noise across twelve cells (green zeros, blue hashed slopes, amber quintic blend, dashed red linear blend with creases), the three fades described in the caption; cite Perlin 1985 SIGGRAPH DOI 10.1145/325165.325247 and Perlin 2002 Improving Noise DOI 10.1145/566654.566636. Viz PerlinNoiseViz: a ten by four window onto a seeded lattice, one cell blended per tick with the hashed gradients in blue and the quintic-faded value in grey, then three ticks adding octaves two to four; invariant every tick: exactly zero at all 55 lattice points through every octave and every sample inside the scaled bound; NODE-VERIFIED 20 cycles x 43 ticks, 0 breaks (501,760 samples per cycle); stepMs 320, holdTicks rests. Preserved narration: Aoede + Algieba, plan 24,388 billable characters (12,194 spoken per voice), 8 requests, $0.731640, approval c106075fde32fd9cbf68771828a09dd0b7e9c2d0184d41cfb95c9c47f6af0277 (not generated yet). units.oneLiner: Draw every trial's hyperparameters independently and uniformly (log-uniform across orders of magnitude), train, keep the best: n trials hit the top 5% of the space with probability 1 - 0.95^n in any dimension, and because only a few knobs matter, n random trials try n values of the one that does where a grid of the same size tries k.
units.description: Random search against the 1 - 0.95^n theorem (0.954 measured at 60 trials), grids, and Latin hypercubes: a k x k grid tries k values of the knob that matters, reaching 0.35, 0.92, 0.40 of the optimum at k = 3, 4, 5; a 15,625-point six-knob grid 0.41 against 0.96 for 60 random trials; a ridge learner within 5% of optimum in 91% and 99% of repeats.
units.plan_row: Random search × Uniform hyperparameter sampling. Puzzle 192, ml-ai (problemSlug hyperparameter-tuning, the atlas problem page carrying "Hyperparameter tuning"; topic model-selection, tier 1; sibling live lessons hill-climbing-random-restarts, puzzle 178, and annealing-cooling, puzzle 2). Solution random_search_uniform_hyperparameter_sampling.py (2.9 s, prints OK, deterministic across runs): uniform, full-factorial grid, and Latin hypercube samplers; a two-dimensional objective with one important axis (peak of width 0.12 at x = 0.37, weak y) and its six-dimensional extension; a top-5%-by-volume threshold (400 x 400 grid in 2-D, 200,000 samples in 6-D) with hit probabilities and standard errors; a Chebyshev-feature polynomial ridge learner (14 training, 200 validation points; knobs degree 1-10, lambda 1e-7 to 1e2 log scale, and one knob the closed-form solver ignores) with a Gaussian-elimination solver; and a closed-form gradient-descent loss on curvatures 1 to 100. ORACLES: (1) THEOREM: P(top 5% hit by n draws) = 0.4080 +/- 0.0049, 0.7793 +/- 0.0041, 0.9539 +/- 0.0021 at n = 10, 30, 60 over 10,000 repeats against 1 - 0.95^n = 0.4013, 0.7854, 0.9539 (each within 3 SE); (2) LOW EFFECTIVE DIMENSIONALITY, 300 repeats: k x k grid = exactly k distinct x values, best/optimum 0.349, 0.916, 0.404, 0.944, 0.916, 0.802 at k = 3..8 (falls 4 to 5 and 7 to 8: alignment lottery, asserted); k^2 random trials = k^2 distinct x, 0.768 +/- 0.014, 0.884, 0.919, 0.950, 0.967, 0.972 +/- 0.001 (rises, beats the grid by > 0.2 at k = 3 and 5, asserted); Latin hypercube 0.885, 0.926, 0.955, 0.966, 0.969, 0.976; (3) LEARNER: dense scan of 3,610 settings, optimum validation MSE 0.0521 at degree 3, lambda 0.0596; within-5% region = 8.5% of the space, so the theorem predicts hit rates 0.91 (27) and 1.00 (64); measured over 200 repeats: random 0.91 and 0.99 (mean best/opt 1.033 +/- 0.009, 1.004 +/- 0.001), LHS 0.98 and 1.00 (1.007 +/- 0.003, 1.002); grid 3 per axis: 9 distinct (degree, lambda) pairs of 27 trainings, 4.915x optimum, miss; grid 4 per axis: 16 of 64, 1.430x, miss (all asserted; random hit rate within 3 SE + 0.03 of 1 - (1 - 0.085)^n; LHS hits at least as often as random); (4) LEARNING RATE on [1e-5, 1], stable below 0.020, best 0.0194 (loss 1.13e-2), 20 draws x 2,000 repeats: uniform converging 0.0195 +/- 0.0007 (theory 0.0200), any convergent draw 0.315, a draw within 2x of the best rate 0.168 (theory 0.187), median best loss/opt 8.5; log-uniform 0.6585 +/- 0.0024 (theory 0.6602), 1.000, 0.721 (theory 0.728), 3.9 (all four closed forms asserted within 3 SE); (5) NEGATIVE EXAMPLE: 5^6 = 15,625-training grid, 5 distinct values per knob, best 0.415 of the six-knob optimum; 60 random trainings 0.963 +/- 0.001 (above 0.9 in 97% of 500 repeats), top-5% hit probability 0.956 +/- 0.003 (theory 0.9539). Two author corrections recorded in the header: the loss-window criterion (0.07 vs 0.27, exponentially sensitive loss) replaced by the rate window; the 40-point draft learner (everything hit the 5% band) replaced by 14 points (band = 8.5% of the space). A measured Gaussian-process expected-improvement rival (95% within 5% at 27, 1.025 +/- 0.020, a draw with random) was authored and then REMOVED to fit the 20 KB page-chunk budget (its GP code alone cost about 1 KB gzipped); the Bayesian optimization card is now qualitative, like Vickrey's VCG card. Cards: self, Grid search, Latin hypercube sampling, Bayesian optimization × Expected improvement (algoName Expected improvement, unmeasured); all algo pages exist. neverUse: an exhaustive grid when six knobs each get five values (15,625 trainings at 0.415 against 60 random at 0.963). Contest: the ridge learner at budgets 27 and 64 (five rows, LHS best at 27). Figure: the Bergstra-Bengio projection picture (4 x 4 grid vs 16 random points, the peak band in green, ticks on the x axis showing 4 against 16 distinct values; the 1 - 0.95^n curve panel was dropped for the chunk budget); cites Bergstra and Bengio JMLR 13 (2012), Li et al. Hyperband JMLR 18 (2018), Snoek, Larochelle, Adams NeurIPS 2012, McKay, Beckman, Conover Technometrics 1979. Viz RandomSearchViz: grid vs random on the same hidden objective, one trial per tick per panel, k seeded 3 to 7, distinct-x counters, best-so-far rings, invariant (equal trial counts, unit square, monotone bests, grid distinct x <= k, end recount equals both bests); NODE-VERIFIED 20 cycles, 0 breaks, 30.25 ticks per cycle; stepMs 400, holdTicks rests. units.oneLiner: Cut the address into offset, index, and tag, let the index pick one small set, and compare only that set's W tags in parallel: the direct-mapped cache's one-step lookup with room for W colliding lines, so a few ways erase most conflict misses (2,357 to 381 at four ways on a Zipf trace, 6,144 to 192 on three aligned arrays) while a stride that aims a hundred blocks at one set still needs tiling or full associativity.
units.description: A 16 KB cache at 1 to 256 ways against two independent references (206,976 agreements), 240,000 bit-exact address rebuilds, and Belady's floor: three arrays one cache size apart miss 6,144 of 6,144 direct-mapped and two-way but 192 four-way; a column walk misses 100% below full associativity, 12.5% tiled; Zipf conflicts 2,357, 990, 381, 201, 0.
units.time: O(W) tag compares per access, in parallel: one step
units.space: capacity plus tag, valid, and recency bits (3.71% to 6.84% here)
units.plan_row: Set-associative cache × Index-tag lookup. Puzzle 194, languages-compilers (problemSlug cache-organization, the atlas problem page carrying "Cache organization"; sibling live lesson lru-recency-eviction, puzzle 17, named in the narration; rivals Victim cache and Skewed-associative cache share the d phrase). Solution set_associative_cache_index_tag_lookup.py (0.7 s, prints OK): a set-associative simulator parameterized by capacity, block, ways, and policy (LRU, FIFO, random) that splits each address into tag, index, and offset and compares one set's tags; a dictionary direct-mapped reference; an ordered-dictionary fully associative LRU reference; Belady optimal with a heap of next uses; the three C decomposition; traces: a 64 KB sequential sweep, three 4 KB arrays spaced 16 KB apart over four passes, a 128 x 128 matrix of doubles by rows, by columns, and in 16-row tiles, a Zipf trace (40,000 accesses, 4,096 blocks, s = 1.0, hot blocks scattered), and a five-block cycle in one four-way set. ORACLES: (1) the fields reconstruct every address bit for bit in 240,000 checks, index bits = log2(sets), offset bits = log2(block), tag the rest (18/8/6 direct-mapped, 20/6/6 four-way, 26/0/6 fully associative); (2) the general simulator equals the direct-mapped reference at W = 1 and the fully associative LRU reference at S = 1 on 206,976 decisions over every trace; (3) Belady misses no more than any configuration on any trace; (4) misses = compulsory + capacity + conflict, conflict 0 when fully associative; (5) measured: sweep and row walk 12.5% everywhere (compulsory only); three arrays (192 of 256 blocks fit) direct-mapped 6,144 of 6,144, 2-way 6,144, 4-way 192 (first touches), 32 KB direct-mapped still 67.7%; column walk 100% at 1, 2, 4, 8, 16 ways, 12.5% fully associative, 12.5% direct-mapped in 16-row tiles; Zipf miss rates 48.05 / 44.63 / 43.11 / 42.66 / 42.52 / 42.16% at 1 / 2 / 4 / 8 / 16 / 256 ways, compulsory 3,535, capacity 13,328, conflict 2,357 / 990 / 381 / 201 / 146 / 0, Belady 10,282 misses (25.70%); rule of thumb direct-mapped 16 KB 19,220 against two-way 8 KB 21,524 (ratio 0.893); replacement at 4 ways on Zipf LRU 17,244, FIFO 18,760, random 18,798; five blocks cycling one four-way set: LRU 10,000 of 10,000, FIFO 10,000, random 4,014, Belady 2,503, four blocks LRU 4; comparators 1 / 2 / 4 / 8 / 16 / 256 per access, tag + valid + LRU overhead 3.71 / 4.10 / 4.49 / 4.88 / 5.27 / 6.84% of data bits. Honest: ways do not fix a stride (said in the weakness and the negative example); LRU loses to random on the five-block cycle. Two author corrections recorded (associativity below full does not rescue the column walk; the three arrays fit three to a set, so four ways miss only first touches, not one in eight). Cards: self, Victim cache, Skewed-associative cache, Loop tiling (all algoName, pages present). neverUse: a direct-mapped cache under streams spaced a cache size apart. Figure: the 32-bit address split for direct-mapped, four-way, and fully associative beside a bar chart of Zipf conflict misses by ways; cite Hill and Smith 1989 DOI 10.1109/12.40842, Smith 1982 DOI 10.1145/356887.356892, Hennessy and Patterson appendix B. Viz SetAssociativeCacheViz: an eight-block cache as 8 x 1, 4 x 2, or 2 x 4 by cycle serving three arrays one cache size apart for two passes (96 accesses), one access per tick, address bits colored by field, the indexed set outlined, hit and miss flashes, counters for hits, misses, and tag compares; invariant: an independent per-set LRU reference agrees on every access and the fields rebuild the address, and at the end direct-mapped and two-way missed everything while four-way missed only the six first touches; NODE-VERIFIED 20 cycles, 96 ticks each, 0 breaks; stepMs 380, holdTicks rests. Preserved narration: Aoede + Algieba, plan 0.733260 USD, 24,442 billable characters, 8 requests (narration trimmed to about 12,100 spoken characters and the page chunk to an estimated 18.9 KB gz after the coordinator's budget note). units.oneLiner: Count each symbol, divide by n, and plug the frequencies into Shannon's formula: one pass, nothing to tune, and a bias that is always negative and known to first order, (k − 1)/(2n ln 2) bits, so that at ten samples per symbol one added term makes it honest and at one sample per symbol nothing does.
units.description: The plug-in entropy estimator against its exact expectation: bias −0.0728 bits at n = 1,000 for 100 equiprobable symbols (Miller −0.0714), −0.00715 at 10,000, −3.41 at n = 10; Miller-Madow and the jackknife erase it at n ≫ k; a 2,000-symbol tail at n = 2,000 sits 0.583 bits low; independent variables show 0.0587 bits of plug-in mutual information.
units.time: O(n + k) per estimate: one pass over the samples, one over the counts
units.baseline: Compressed size per symbol (Huffman on the counts)
units.plan_row: Shannon entropy estimation × Maximum likelihood plug-in. Puzzle 195, compression-coding (problemSlug entropy-estimation, the atlas problem page carrying "Entropy estimation"; sibling live lesson huffman-frequency-merges). Solution shannon_entropy_estimation_maximum_likelihood_plug_in.py (0.7 s, prints OK, 62 assertions): the plug-in in its log n form, Miller-Madow and jackknife corrections, the EXACT expectation of the plug-in as a sum of binomial terms (a brute force over every count vector on a 4-symbol alphabet at n = 8 agrees to 1e-12: 1.532790 bits against a truth of 1.846439), a Huffman coder on the counts, Zipf distributions, and a plug-in mutual information. ORACLES: (1) 100 equiprobable symbols (6.644 bits): exact bias -3.41 at n = 10 (E[plug-in] 3.233, log2 10 = 3.322), -2.01 at 30, -0.822 at 100 (Miller first-order -0.714), -0.261 at 300, -0.0728 at 1,000 (-0.0714), -0.0239 at 3,000, -0.00715 at 10,000 (-0.00714); Miller-Madow -2.79, -1.40, -0.370, -0.034, -0.0012 (exact -0.00136), -0.0001, -0.0000; jackknife -2.12, -0.83, -0.065, +0.027, +0.0018, +0.0002, -0.0000; sd 0.0101 at 1,000 and 0.0009 at 10,000 (ratio 11.06: the uniform leading variance term vanishes, 1/n). Instance: a query of 80 bases against 328 sequences of 160 (200 random decoys, 128 planted homologs, 16 per divergence from 5% to 40%, with indels); +5/-4, gap -6, X-drop 40; thresholds one above the best decoy for every method (zero false positives on the 200 decoys). ORACLES: every HSP recounts from its extents and never exceeds the Smith-Waterman score or the exact ungapped maximum of its pair; Smith-Waterman finds every homolog to 25% and at least as many as seeding at every level (121 of 128 in all); sensitivity falls from w = 7 (105) to 11 (74) to 15 (54); the gapped stage (74) sits between the ungapped search and the referee; two-hit extends less (31 against 92 extensions, 31 found); w = 4 fires more than ten times the hits (20,101 against 1,144; 410,736 cells against 5,408; 10x against 776x); w = 11 spends under a hundredth of the referee's 4,198,400 cells; fitted lambda 0.197 within 30% of Karlin-Altschul 0.192 (K 0.1540, 500 fresh null sequences); at T2 = 54 the fit predicts 9.1 chance decoys and 13 appear, within 2.5 sigma; no decoy admitted by any method (ungapped T = 66 with fitted E-value 1.44 per search, gapped T = 107); the same top hit (sequence 25, 10% divergence); all 75 banded scores equal the full Smith-Waterman score (102,000 cells); every one of the 47 w = 11 misses shares no eleven-base word with the query (0 weak segments, 0 short extensions); 69 of 74 HSPs equal the exact best ungapped segment.
